chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the women who perform Tawaf upon camels and beasts of burden; is it sufficient for them to stand beneath As-Safa and Al-Marwa? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, as long as they can see the House.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for women performing Sa'i while riding on camels?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical concessions (rukhas) granted to women during Sa'i, allowing them to remain mounted on camels or beasts of burden rather than walking, provided they can see the Kaaba to maintain spiritual orientation. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as a facilitation for those with physical limitations or for the sake of modesty, distinguishing their requirement from the full physical exertion expected of men. The condition of seeing the Kaaba underscores the importance of visual connection to the sacred center while performing the ritual in a seated or mounted posture.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the women performing Tawaaf upon the camel and the animals, are they allowed to be pausing beneath Al-Safa and Al-Marwa?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, by where they can see the House (Kabah)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of women who perform Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah on camels and stumpers; if they can stop below al-Safa’ and al-Marwah. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, they can do so in a way that they can see the House.’”
